what_its_for: Brexpiprazole is used to treat schizophrenia (a mental health condition that affects how you think, feel, and behave) and major depressive disorder (MDD) when used together with an antidepressant. It may also be used to treat agitation related to Alzheimer's dementia. It works by balancing certain natural chemicals in the brain called dopamine and serotonin.
how_to_take: Take brexpiprazole by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not crush or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find the right dose for you. The usual dose depends on what condition is being treated: for schizophrenia, doses range from 2 mg to 4 mg per day; for major depressive disorder, doses range from 0.5 mg to 3 mg per day. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store brexpiprazole at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Avoid getting too hot or becoming dehydrated, especially in hot weather or during exercise, as this drug can affect your body's ability to regulate temperature. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they may affect how the medication works in your body. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because many drugs can interact with brexpiprazole.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, unusual changes in mood or behavior, high fever, stiff muscles, confusion, or fast heartbeat (signs of a rare but serious condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome), uncontrollable movements of the face, tongue, or body (signs of tardive dyskinesia), fainting or feeling lightheaded when standing up, sudden weight gain or increased hunger and thirst (signs of high blood sugar), signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, seizures, or difficulty swallowing.
when_it_works: You may not feel the full benefits of brexpiprazole right away. Some people notice improvement in symptoms within 1 to 2 weeks, but it may take 4 to 6 weeks or longer to feel the full effect. It is important to keep taking your medication even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause your symptoms to return.
special_populations: Older adults with dementia-related psychosis: This medication carries a serious warning (called a Black Box Warning) because it has been linked to a higher risk of death in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Pregnant women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Babies born to mothers taking this type of medication in the third trimester may have withdrawal symptoms or movement problems after birth. Breastfeeding: It is not known if brexpiprazole passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe kidney or liver problems. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established for all uses.
